uauh.section: From entropic PFR to combinatorial PFR

ah.section: From entropic PFR to combinatorial PFR

nodes.name: Marton's conjecture (polynomial Freiman--Ruzsa conjecture)
nodes.statement: Suppose that $A \subset \mathbf{F}_2^n$ is a set with $|A + A| \leqslant K|A|$. Then $A$ is covered by at most $2 K^{C}$ cosets\footnote{The factor of $2$ is needed to deal with the case where $K$ is close to $1$. If $H_0$ is a subgroup of $\mathbf{F}_2^n$ and $A \subseteq H_0$ is a subset of size $(1-\varepsilon)|H_0|$ for some small $\varepsilon>0$, then in order to obtain the bound $|H|\leqslant|A|$, we need to pick a subgroup $H$ of $H_0$ of index 2 and cover $A$ by the two cosets of that subgroup.} of some subgroup $H \leqslant \mathbf{F}_2^n$ of size at most $|A|$.
assumptions: $A \subset \mathbf{F}_2^n$ is a set with $|A + A| \leqslant K|A|$
conclusions: $A$ is covered by at most $2 K^{C}$ cosets
nodes.statement_short: A subset of $\mathbf{F}_2^n$ with doubling $K$ is covered by $2K^C$ cosets of a subgroup of size at most $|A|$.
nodes.label: pfr-conj

nodes.name: Converse of the PFR conjecture
nodes.statement: Note that if $A$ is covered by at most $r$ cosets of a subgroup $H$ of size at most $|A|$, then $|A+A|\leqslant (\binom r2+1)|A|$, so \Cref{pfr-conj} allows one to pass from the property of having a small doubling constant to the property of being contained in a small union of cosets of a subgroup of size at most $|A|$ and back again with at most a polynomial loss in the parameters.
assumptions: $A$ is covered by at most $r$ cosets of a subgroup $H$ of size at most $|A|$
conclusions: $|A+A|\leqslant (\binom r2+1)|A|$
nodes.statement_short: Covering by $r$ cosets of a small subgroup forces doubling at most $\binom r2+1$, so PFR is an equivalence up to polynomial loss.

nodes.name: Ruzsa's bound for Marton's conjecture
nodes.statement: The first result in this direction was due to Imre Ruzsa~\cite{ruzsa-fin-field}, who obtained an upper bound of $2K^2 2^{K^4}$ in place of the desired $2K^C$.
conclusions: an upper bound of $2K^2 2^{K^4}$ in place of the desired $2K^C$

nodes.name: Sanders' quasi-polynomial Freiman--Ruzsa bound
nodes.statement: Sanders~\cite{sanders} made a dramatic breakthrough by proving the first bounds of shape $\ll \exp(\log^{C_1} K)$, showing that $C_1 = 4 + \varepsilon$ is permissible here.
conclusions: bounds of shape $\ll \exp(\log^{C_1} K)$
$C_1 = 4 + \varepsilon$ is permissible

nodes.name: Konyagin's improvement of Sanders' bound
nodes.statement: A variant of Sanders' argument due to Konyagin (not published by Konyagin, but described by Sanders in~\cite{sanders2}, and see also the comments on page 8 of~\cite{gmt}) showed that $C_1 = 3 + \varepsilon$ is permissible.
conclusions: $C_1 = 3 + \varepsilon$ is permissible

nodes.name: PFR conjecture for downsets
nodes.statement: We also remark that \Cref{pfr-conj} (with worse values of $C$) was previously established in the special case when $A$ was a downset in~\cite{gt-freiman}.
conclusions: \Cref{pfr-conj} (with worse values of $C$) was previously established

nodes.name: Marton's conjecture with C = 12
nodes.statement: \Cref{pfr-conj} is true with $C = 12$.
conclusions: \Cref{pfr-conj} is true with $C = 12$.
nodes.label: pfr

nodes.name: Liao's refinement C = 11
nodes.statement: Since the initial release of this preprint, Jyun-Jie Liao has given a refinement of the argument that improves the constant $C=12$ in \Cref{pfr} to $C=11$ (with corresponding numerical improvements to our other main results and applications); see~\cite{liao1,liao2}.
conclusions: improves the constant $C=12$ in \Cref{pfr} to $C=11$

nodes.name: Proof of the weak PFR conjecture over Z
nodes.statement: It was shown in~\cite[Theorem 1.11]{gmt} that \Cref{pfr-entropy} (or \Cref{pfr}) in characteristic $2$ implies the so-called `weak' polynomial Freiman--Ruzsa conjecture over $\mathbf{Z}$, so that is now a theorem as well.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the implication of [GMT, Thm 1.11] with the entropic PFR theorem.

nodes.name: Weak polynomial Freiman--Ruzsa conjecture over Z
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be a finite subset of $\mathbf{Z}^D$ for some $D$, and suppose that $|A+A| \leqslant K|A|$. Then there is some set $A' \subseteq A$, $|A'| \geqslant K^{-C_1/2} |A|$, with $\dim A' \leqslant C_2 \log K$, for some absolute\footnote{If one traces through the arguments in~\cite{gmt} (dropping all terms involving the exponent $1-1/C_{\mathrm{PFR}}$, and using the constant $C=11$ from \Cref{pfr-entropy} below), one finds that one can take $C_1 = 20C = 220$ and $C_2 = \frac{40}{\log 2}$. The reason we have stated \Cref{th13} with a $C_1/2$ in the exponent is so that the constants $C_1, C_2$ here are the same as the ones in~\cite{gmt}.} constants $C_1,C_2>0$.
assumptions: $A$ be a finite subset of $\mathbf{Z}^D$ for some $D$
conclusions: there is some set $A' \subseteq A$, $|A'| \geqslant K^{-C_1/2} |A|$, with $\dim A' \leqslant C_2 \log K$
nodes.statement_short: A set of integers with doubling $K$ has a $K^{-O(1)}$-dense subset of dimension $O(\log K)$.
nodes.label: th13

nodes.name: Strong PFR conjecture over Z
nodes.statement: We remark that there is also a `strong' PFR conjecture over $\mathbf{Z}$ (though its formulation requires care; see~\cite{lovett-regev} and~\cite{manners-pfr-formulation} for more discussion). This remains a challenging open problem.

nodes.name: Additive stability (approximate homomorphisms with small defect set)
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C_3$ such that if $f: \mathbf{F}_2^m \to \mathbf{F}_2^n$ is a function such that the set $\{ f(x)+f(y)-f(x+y): x,y \in \mathbf{F}_2^m\}$ has cardinality at most $K$, then $f$ may be written as $g+h$, where $g$ is linear and the range of $h$ is a set of cardinality $O(K^{C_3})$.
assumptions: $f: \mathbf{F}_2^m \to \mathbf{F}_2^n$ is a function such that the set $\{ f(x)+f(y)-f(x+y): x,y \in \mathbf{F}_2^m\}$ has cardinality at most $K$
conclusions: $f$ may be written as $g+h$, where $g$ is linear and the range of $h$ is a set of cardinality $O(K^{C_3})$
nodes.label: additive-stability

nodes.name: Proof of additive stability (Ruzsa's equivalence)
nodes.statement: The equivalence of this and \Cref{pfr} is due to Ruzsa~\cite[Conjecture 2.2.3]{ruzsa-sumsets-survey}. Ruzsa did not publish the proof, but he communicated it to the second author and the details may be found in~\cite{green-pfr-note}.
nodes.statement_short: Follows from Theorem 1.2 via Ruzsa's equivalence, detailed in Green's note.

nodes.name: Big-O notation
nodes.statement: Here, as usual, $O(X)$ denotes a quantity bounded by $CX$ for some absolute constant~$C$.
differentia: bounded by $CX$ for some absolute constant~$C$

nodes.name: Linearity testing at large distances
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C_4$ with the following property. Suppose that $f : \mathbf{F}_2^m \to \mathbf{F}_2^n$ is a function such that, if $x, y$ are selected uniformly at random from $\mathbf{F}_2^m$, $\mathbf{P}(f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y)) \geqslant 1/K$. Then there is a homomorphism $g \colon \mathbf{F}_2^m \to \mathbf{F}_2^n$ such that $\mathbf{P}(f(x) = g(x)) \gg K^{-C_4}$.
assumptions: $f : \mathbf{F}_2^m \to \mathbf{F}_2^n$ is a function such that, if $x, y$ are selected uniformly at random from $\mathbf{F}_2^m$, $\mathbf{P}(f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y)) \geqslant 1/K$
conclusions: there is a homomorphism $g \colon \mathbf{F}_2^m \to \mathbf{F}_2^n$ such that $\mathbf{P}(f(x) = g(x)) \gg K^{-C_4}$
nodes.statement_short: A function that is additive with probability $1/K$ agrees with a homomorphism on a $K^{-O(1)}$ fraction.
nodes.label: partial-additivity

nodes.name: Proof of the linearity-testing corollary (citation)
nodes.statement: See~\cite[Theorem 4.1]{samorodnitsky}.
nodes.statement_short: Deduced from PFR via Samorodnitsky's Theorem 4.1.

nodes.name: Vinogradov notation
nodes.statement: The notation $X\gg Y$ means that there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that $X\geqslant cY$.

nodes.name: Proof of the polynomial U^3 inverse theorem (citation)
nodes.statement: The next result is a polynomially effective inverse theorem for the Gowers uniformity norm ${U^3(\mathbf{F}_2^n)}$; see~\cite{gt-equiv, lovett, samorodnitsky}.
nodes.statement_short: Deduced from PFR via the cited equivalences of Green--Tao, Lovett and Samorodnitsky.

nodes.name: Polynomial inverse theorem for the Gowers U^3 norm
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C_5$ with the following property. Let $f \colon \mathbf{F}_2^n \to \mathbf{C}$ be a $1$-bounded function such that $\|f\|_{U^3(\mathbf{F}_2^n)} \geqslant 1/K$. Then there exists a quadratic polynomial $P \colon \mathbf{F}_2^n \to \mathbf{F}_2$ such that \[ |\frac{1}{2^n} \sum_{x \in \mathbf{F}_2^n} f(x) (-1)^{P(x)}| \gg K^{-C_5}.\]
conclusions: there exists a quadratic polynomial $P \colon \mathbf{F}_2^n \to \mathbf{F}_2$ such that \[ |\frac{1}{2^n} \sum_{x \in \mathbf{F}_2^n} f(x) (-1)^{P(x)}| \gg K^{-C_5}.\]
nodes.statement_short: A bounded function with large $U^3$ norm correlates polynomially with a quadratic phase.
nodes.label: u3-inverse

nodes.name: Mudgal's sum-product theorem
nodes.statement: Let $A \subset \mathbf{R}$ be a finite set with at least two elements. Then either then $m$-fold sumset $mA$ or the $m$-fold product set $A^{(m)}$ has cardinality at least $|A|^{f(m)}$, where $f(m) \rightarrow \infty$ as $m \rightarrow \infty$.
assumptions: $A \subset \mathbf{R}$ be a finite set with at least two elements
conclusions: either then $m$-fold sumset $mA$ or the $m$-fold product set $A^{(m)}$ has cardinality at least $|A|^{f(m)}$, where $f(m) \rightarrow \infty$ as $m \rightarrow \infty$

nodes.name: Bourgain--Chang sum-product theorem
nodes.statement: This generalizes a well-known result of Bourgain and Chang~\cite{bourgain-chang}, who established this when $A$ is a set of integers.

nodes.name: Entropic Ruzsa distance
nodes.statement: If $X, Y$ are two finitely supported random variables taking values in an additive group $G$, then we define \begin{equation} \dist{X}{Y} \coloneqq \ent{X' - Y'} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X'} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{Y'}, \end{equation} where $X', Y'$ are independent copies of $X, Y$.
differentia: where $X', Y'$ are independent copies of $X, Y$
nodes.statement_short: Ruzsa distance: entropy of the difference of independent copies minus half of each entropy.

nodes.name: Ruzsa distance formula (1.1)
nodes.statement: \dist{X}{Y} \coloneqq \ent{X' - Y'} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X'} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{Y'},
nodes.label: ruz-dist-def

nodes.name: Entropic polynomial Freiman--Ruzsa theorem
nodes.statement: Let $G = \mathbf{F}_2^n$, and suppose that $X^0_1, X^0_2$ are $G$-valued random variables. Then there is some subgroup $H \leqslant G$ such that \[ \dist{X^0_1}{U_H} + \dist{X^0_2}{U_H} \leqslant 11\dist{X^0_1}{X^0_2}, \] where $U_H$ denotes the uniform distribution on $H$. Furthermore, both $\dist{X^0_1}{U_H}$ and $\dist{X^0_2}{U_H}$ are at most $6 \dist{X^0_1}{X^0_2}$.
conclusions: there is some subgroup $H \leqslant G$ such that \[ \dist{X^0_1}{U_H} + \dist{X^0_2}{U_H} \leqslant 11\dist{X^0_1}{X^0_2}, \]
both $\dist{X^0_1}{U_H}$ and $\dist{X^0_2}{U_H}$ are at most $6 \dist{X^0_1}{X^0_2}$
nodes.statement_short: Any two $\mathbf{F}_2^n$-valued random variables are within $11$ times their Ruzsa distance of a uniform distribution on a subgroup.
nodes.label: pfr-entropy

nodes.name: Equivalence of entropic and combinatorial PFR
nodes.statement: The fact that \Cref{pfr-entropy} is equivalent, up to constants, to the characteristic $2$ case of Marton's original conjecture, as well as to the other combinatorial formulations of the polynomial Freiman--Ruzsa conjecture, was established in~\cite[Section 8]{gmt}.
conclusions: \Cref{pfr-entropy} is equivalent, up to constants, to the characteristic $2$ case of Marton's original conjecture, as well as to the other combinatorial formulations of the polynomial Freiman--Ruzsa conjecture

nodes.name: Strong PFR conjecture
nodes.statement: One could consider strengthening \Cref{additive-stability} by requiring the function $h$ to take values in a $C_7$-fold sumset of the set $\{ f(x)+f(y)-f(x+y): x,y \in \mathbf{F}_2^m\}$, for some absolute constant $C_7$.
nodes.statement_short: Strengthen Corollary 1.4 by asking that $h$ takes values in a bounded iterated sumset of the defect set.

nodes.name: Strong PFR conjecture is false
nodes.statement: However, this ``strong PFR conjecture'' is known to be false: see~\cite{aaronson} and~\cite[Section 1.17]{tao-poincare}.
conclusions: this ``strong PFR conjecture'' is known to be false

nodes.name: Polynomial Bogolyubov conjecture
nodes.statement: The \emph{polynomial Bogolyubov conjecture} (see e.g.,~\cite[Conjecture 1.5]{lovett-survey}) asserts that if $A$ is a non-empty subset of $\mathbf{F}_2^n$ of doubling at most $K$, then $2A-2A=4A$ contains a subspace of cardinality $\gg K^{-O(1)} |A|$.
assumptions: $A$ is a non-empty subset of $\mathbf{F}_2^n$ of doubling at most $K$
conclusions: $2A-2A=4A$ contains a subspace of cardinality $\gg K^{-O(1)} |A|$

nodes.name: Sanders' Bogolyubov--Ruzsa lemma
nodes.statement: In~\cite{sanders} it was shown that $2A-2A$ contains a subspace of size at least $\gg K^{-O(\log^3 K)} |A|$; see also a recent bilinear extension of this result in~\cite{hosseini-lovett}.
conclusions: $2A-2A$ contains a subspace of size at least $\gg K^{-O(\log^3 K)} |A|$

nodes.name: Even-Zohar's bounds for f(2,K)
nodes.statement: Let $f(2,K)$ denote the best constant such that every non-empty subset $A$ of $\mathbf{F}_2^n$ of doubling at most $K$ is contained in an affine subspace of cardinality at most $f(2,K) |A|$. It is known that $f(2,K)$ is a piecewise linear function that can be explicitly computed for small $K$, and has the asymptotic bounds \[ \frac{2^{2K}}{4K} (1-o(1)) \leqslant f(2,K) \leqslant \frac{2^{2K}}{2K}(1+o(1))\] as $K \to \infty$; see~\cite{even-zohar} (which builds upon prior work in~\cite{diao, gt-freiman, konyagin}).
conclusions: $f(2,K)$ is a piecewise linear function that can be explicitly computed for small $K$
\[ \frac{2^{2K}}{4K} (1-o(1)) \leqslant f(2,K) \leqslant \frac{2^{2K}}{2K}(1+o(1))\]
nodes.statement_short: Sharp asymptotics $2^{2K}/K$ up to a factor 2 for the affine-span constant $f(2,K)$ of sets of doubling $K$.

nodes.name: Ambient group and reference variables
nodes.statement: Fix, for the rest of the paper, the group $G = \mathbf{F}_2^n$ and the variables $X^0_1, X^0_2$ appearing in \Cref{pfr-entropy}.

nodes.name: The constant eta
nodes.statement: For the rest of the paper, $\eta$ will denote the constant $\frac{1}{9}$.

nodes.name: The functional tau
nodes.statement: For any two $G$-valued random variables $X_1, X_2$, we introduce the functional \begin{equation} \tau[X_1; X_2] \coloneqq \dist{X_1}{X_2} + \eta \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} + \eta \dist{X^0_2}{X_2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\tau$ = Ruzsa distance of $X_1,X_2$ plus $\eta$-weighted distances to the reference variables.

nodes.name: Definition of tau (2.1)
nodes.statement: \tau[X_1; X_2] \coloneqq \dist{X_1}{X_2} + \eta \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} + \eta \dist{X^0_2}{X_2}.
nodes.label: tau-def

nodes.name: Entropy decrement proposition
nodes.statement: Let $X_1, X_2$ be two $G$-valued random variables with $\dist{X_1}{X_2} > 0$. Then there are $G$-valued random variables $X'_1, X'_2$ such that \begin{equation} \tau[X'_1;X'_2] < \tau[X_1;X_2]. \end{equation}
assumptions: $X_1, X_2$ be two $G$-valued random variables with $\dist{X_1}{X_2} > 0$
conclusions: there are $G$-valued random variables $X'_1, X'_2$ such that \begin{equation} \label{d-opt} \tau[X'_1;X'_2] < \tau[X_1;X_2]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: If $d[X_1;X_2]>0$ one can find a new pair with strictly smaller $\tau$.
nodes.label: de-prop

nodes.name: Interpretation of the decrement proposition
nodes.statement: If we ignore the two penalty terms involving $\eta$ on the right-hand side of~\eqref{tau-def}, then \Cref{de-prop} asserts that if two random variables have a positive Ruzsa distance, then we can `improve' them, finding two new variables $X'_1, X'_2$ that are closer to each other than the original variables $X_1,X_2$. To take care of the penalty terms, we will also need the new variables $X'_1,X'_2$ to be `related' to the old variables $X_1,X_2$ in some sense, so that both sets of variables have a comparable Ruzsa distance to the reference variables $X^0_1, X^0_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Without penalty terms, Prop. 2.1 says variables at positive distance can be moved closer; the penalties keep them related to the references.

nodes.name: 100% case of entropic PFR
nodes.statement: Suppose that $X_1,X_2$ are $G$-valued random variables such that $\dist{X_1}{X_2}=0$. Then there exists a subgroup $H \leqslant G$ such that $\dist{X_1}{U_H} = \dist{X_2}{U_H} = 0$.
conclusions: there exists a subgroup $H \leqslant G$ such that $\dist{X_1}{U_H} = \dist{X_2}{U_H} = 0$
nodes.statement_short: Zero Ruzsa distance forces both variables to be at distance zero from a uniform subgroup distribution.
nodes.label: lem:100pc

nodes.name: Proof of the 100% case
nodes.statement: By the triangle inequality, $\dist{X_1}{X_1} = 0$, and so (since $G=\mathbf{F}_2^n$) we have $\dist{X_1}{-X_1} = 0$. By~\cite[Theorem~1.11(i)]{tao-entropy}, it follows that there exists a subgroup $H$ with $\dist{X_1}{U_H} = 0$. Then $\dist{X_2}{U_H}=0$ follows by the triangle inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality gives $d[X_1;-X_1]=0$; Tao's characterisation yields a subgroup $H$.

nodes.name: Self-distance zero
nodes.statement: By the triangle inequality, $\dist{X_1}{X_1} = 0$, and so (since $G=\mathbf{F}_2^n$) we have $\dist{X_1}{-X_1} = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality gives $d[X_1;X_1]=0=d[X_1;-X_1]$.

nodes.name: Find the subgroup
nodes.statement: By~\cite[Theorem~1.11(i)]{tao-entropy}, it follows that there exists a subgroup $H$ with $\dist{X_1}{U_H} = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Tao's theorem to get a subgroup $H$.

nodes.name: Conclude for X_2
nodes.statement: Then $\dist{X_2}{U_H}=0$ follows by the triangle inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality transfers to $X_2$.

nodes.name: Proof of entropic PFR assuming Proposition 2.1
nodes.statement: We choose a pair of variables $X_1,X_2$ (or more precisely, their distributions on $G$) to be any minimizer\footnote{We remark that an entropy functional minimization was previously employed by the fourth author in~\cite{tao-regularity} to give an alternative proof of the Szemer\'edi regularity lemma.} of the functional $\tau$. This optimization problem ranges over the square of the space of probability distributions on the finite set $G$. The usual topology on this space is compact, and it is straightforward that $\dist{-}{ -}$ is continuous with respect to this topology, so the minimum exists. As $(X_1,X_2)$ minimizes $\tau$, by the contrapositive of \Cref{de-prop} we must have $\dist{X_1}{X_2}=0$, and hence by \Cref{lem:100pc} there exists a subgroup $H \leqslant G$ such that $\dist{X_1}{U_H} = \dist{X_2}{U_H}=0$. Finally, we have \begin{align*} \eta (\dist{X_1^0}{U_H} + & \dist{X_2^0}{U_H})= \eta (\dist{X_1^0}{X_1} + \dist{X_2^0}{X_2}) \\ & = \tau[X_1;X_2] \leqslant \tau[X_2^0;X_1^0] = (1+2\eta) \dist{X_1^0}{X_2^0}, \end{align*} and so with our choice $\eta = \frac{1}{9}$ we obtain the first claim of \Cref{pfr-entropy}. Since $ \lvert \dist{X^0_1}{U_H} - \dist{X^0_2}{U_H} \rvert \leqslant \dist{X^0_1}{X^0_2} $ by the triangle inequality, the second statement then follows.
nodes.statement_short: Compactness: take a minimiser of $\tau$; Prop. 2.1 forces $d=0$, Lemma 2.2 gives $H$, then compare $\tau$ with its value at the reference pair.

nodes.name: Choose a minimiser
nodes.statement: We choose a pair of variables $X_1,X_2$ (or more precisely, their distributions on $G$) to be any minimizer\footnote{We remark that an entropy functional minimization was previously employed by the fourth author in~\cite{tao-regularity} to give an alternative proof of the Szemer\'edi regularity lemma.} of the functional $\tau$. This optimization problem ranges over the square of the space of probability distributions on the finite set $G$. The usual topology on this space is compact, and it is straightforward that $\dist{-}{ -}$ is continuous with respect to this topology, so the minimum exists.
nodes.statement_short: Take a minimiser of $\tau$, which exists by compactness.

nodes.name: Apply decrement and 100% case
nodes.statement: As $(X_1,X_2)$ minimizes $\tau$, by the contrapositive of \Cref{de-prop} we must have $\dist{X_1}{X_2}=0$, and hence by \Cref{lem:100pc} there exists a subgroup $H \leqslant G$ such that $\dist{X_1}{U_H} = \dist{X_2}{U_H}=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Minimality and Prop. 2.1 give $d=0$; Lemma 2.2 gives $H$.

nodes.name: First bound
nodes.statement: Finally, we have \begin{align*} \eta (\dist{X_1^0}{U_H} + & \dist{X_2^0}{U_H})= \eta (\dist{X_1^0}{X_1} + \dist{X_2^0}{X_2}) \\ & = \tau[X_1;X_2] \leqslant \tau[X_2^0;X_1^0] = (1+2\eta) \dist{X_1^0}{X_2^0}, \end{align*} and so with our choice $\eta = \frac{1}{9}$ we obtain the first claim of \Cref{pfr-entropy}.
nodes.statement_short: Compare $\tau$ at the minimiser with $\tau[X_2^0;X_1^0]$ to get the factor 11.

nodes.name: Second bound
nodes.statement: Since $ \lvert \dist{X^0_1}{U_H} - \dist{X^0_2}{U_H} \rvert \leqslant \dist{X^0_1}{X^0_2} $ by the triangle inequality, the second statement then follows.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality gives the second claim.

nodes.name: Algorithmic variant of the argument
nodes.statement: The proof of \Cref{de-prop} is completely algorithmic, but our use of compactness here means that the proof of \Cref{pfr-entropy} is not. However, our argument can be modified to give a completely algorithmic proof, at the expense of slightly worse constants. One approach is to prove \Cref{de-prop} with~\eqref{d-opt} replaced by the stronger bound \begin{equation} \dist{X'_1}{X'_2} \leqslant (1 - \eta') \dist{X_1}{X_2} - \eta' \dist{X'_1}{X_1} - \eta' \dist{X'_2}{X_2}, \end{equation} for some value $\eta'$ rather smaller than $\eta=\frac{1}{9}$. The proof is very similar and follows the same strategy as that outlined in \Cref{sec3}. This variant is perhaps even slightly easier to follow than the current proof, since the `fixed' variables $X_1^0, X_2^0$ no longer play a role. Once~\eqref{proper-decrement} is established, it can be applied iteratively to give a sequence $(X_1^{t}, X_2^{t})$, $t = 0,1,\dots$ for which $\dist{X_1^{t}}{X_2^{t}}$ decays exponentially. In particular, for some $T = O(\log \dist{X^0_1}{X^0_2})$ we have $\dist{X_1^{T}}{X_2^{T}} \leqslant \varepsilon_0$, where $\varepsilon_0$ is the absolute constant appearing in~\cite[Proposition 1.3]{gmt}. By that result, $X_1^{T}$ and $X_2^{T}$ are both close to some variable $U_H$. One can then control the distance of $U_H$ from the original variables $X^0_1, X^0_2$ by summing~\eqref{proper-decrement} over $0 \leqslant t < T$ and applying the Ruzsa triangle inequality repeatedly. A version of this argument will be given in detail in our subsequent paper~\cite{ggmt-pfr-odd}.
nodes.statement_short: Proving a proper decrement (2.3) instead of (2.2) gives an iterative, non-compactness proof with worse constants.
nodes.label: quant

nodes.name: Proper decrement inequality (2.3)
nodes.statement: \dist{X'_1}{X'_2} \leqslant (1 - \eta') \dist{X_1}{X_2} - \eta' \dist{X'_1}{X_1} - \eta' \dist{X'_2}{X_2},
nodes.label: proper-decrement

nodes.name: Weak Bogolyubov-type consequence
nodes.statement: We sketch one further consequence of the variant argument discussed in \Cref{quant} above, namely a weak Bogulyubov-type result: if $|A+A| \leqslant K|A|$, then there is a subspace $H$ of $G$ of cardinality $\gg K^{-O(1)} |A|$ that is contained in an iterated sumset $mA$ for some $m = O(\log^{O(1)}(2+K))$. Indeed, if takes $X^0_1 = X^0_2 = U_A$ as in \Cref{equiv-app} and runs the above iteration, we see inductively from an inspection of the construction that each pair $X_1^t, X_2^t$ of random variables produced by the iterative process is contained in $m_t A$ for some $m_t = O(1)^t$. Since it only takes $O(\log\log K)$ steps for the doubling constant to get within range of $\varepsilon_0$, one can check (by inspection of the argument in~\cite[Proposition 1.3]{gmt}) that the group $H$ produced is then contained in $mA$ for some $m = O(\log^{O(1)}(2+K))$, and the claim then follows after some routine verifications.
nodes.statement_short: The iterative variant shows a subspace of size $K^{-O(1)}|A|$ lies in $mA$ with $m$ polylogarithmic in $K$.
nodes.label: bog-remark

nodes.name: The quantity k
nodes.statement: Let $k$ denote the quantity $k \coloneqq \dist{X_1}{X_2}$.

nodes.name: Informal O(eta k) notation
nodes.statement: For the following preliminary discussion we write various estimates as $O(\eta k)$ for simplicity.

nodes.name: Independent copies tilde X_1, tilde X_2
nodes.statement: To describe the choices we will try, consider a four-tuple of independent random variables $X_1, X_2, \tilde X_1, \tilde X_2$ where $X_1,\tilde X_1$ are copies of $X_1$ and $X_2,\tilde X_2$ are copies of $X_2$; we can in fact assume that all six variables $X_1,X_2,\tilde X_1,\tilde X_2,X^0_1,X^0_2$ are independent.

nodes.name: Candidate choices: sums and fibres
nodes.statement: Our primary choices for $(X'_1, X'_2)$ will be sums \begin{equation} X'_1 = X_1 + \tilde X_2,\qquad X'_2 = X_2 + \tilde X_1 \end{equation} or \begin{equation} X'_1 = X_1 + \tilde X_1,\qquad X'_2 = X_2 + \tilde X_2 \end{equation} or alternatively `fibres' \begin{equation} X'_1 = (X_1 | X_1 + \tilde X_2= g),\qquad X'_2 = (X_2 | X_2 + \tilde X_1 = g') \end{equation} or \begin{equation} X'_1 = (X_1 | X_1 + \tilde X_1= g),\qquad X'_2 = (X_2 | X_2 + \tilde X_2 = g') \end{equation} for $g, g' \in G$.
nodes.statement_short: Candidates for $(X'_1,X'_2)$: the sums (3.1), (3.2) and the fibres (3.3), (3.4).

nodes.name: Sum choice (3.1)
nodes.statement: X'_1 = X_1 + \tilde X_2,\qquad X'_2 = X_2 + \tilde X_1
nodes.label: sum-1

nodes.name: Sum choice (3.2)
nodes.statement: X'_1 = X_1 + \tilde X_1,\qquad X'_2 = X_2 + \tilde X_2
nodes.label: sum-2

nodes.name: Fibre choice (3.3)
nodes.statement: X'_1 = (X_1 | X_1 + \tilde X_2= g),\qquad X'_2 = (X_2 | X_2 + \tilde X_1 = g')
nodes.label: fiber-1

nodes.name: Fibre choice (3.4)
nodes.statement: X'_1 = (X_1 | X_1 + \tilde X_1= g),\qquad X'_2 = (X_2 | X_2 + \tilde X_2 = g')
nodes.label: fiber-2

nodes.name: Heuristic first estimate
nodes.statement: What we find in this case is that if neither choice~\eqref{sum-1},~\eqref{fiber-1} works to prove~\eqref{d-opt} then we have an upper bound \begin{equation} I_1 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } = O(\eta k). \end{equation}
conclusions: I_1 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } = O(\eta k).
nodes.statement_short: If sum and fibre choices (3.1), (3.3) fail, the conditional mutual information $I_1$ is $O(\eta k)$.

nodes.name: Definition and heuristic bound of I_1 (3.5)
nodes.statement: I_1 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } = O(\eta k).
nodes.label: first-est-a

nodes.name: Heuristic second estimate
nodes.statement: Similarly, if neither choice~\eqref{sum-2},~\eqref{fiber-2} works to prove~\eqref{d-opt}, we obtain a bound \begin{equation} I_2 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } = O(\eta k). \end{equation}
conclusions: I_2 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } = O(\eta k).
nodes.statement_short: If choices (3.2), (3.4) fail, $I_2$ is $O(\eta k)$.

nodes.name: Definition and heuristic bound of I_2 (3.6)
nodes.statement: I_2 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } = O(\eta k).
nodes.label: second-est-a

nodes.name: Heuristic third estimate
nodes.statement: Finally, \begin{equation} I_3 \coloneqq \bigI{ \tilde X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } = O(\eta k), \end{equation} since in fact we have $I_2 = I_3$, as may be seen by interchanging the names of $\tilde X_1$ and $X_1$.
conclusions: I_3 \coloneqq \bigI{ \tilde X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } = O(\eta k),
nodes.statement_short: $I_3$ is $O(\eta k)$ too, because $I_2 = I_3$ by symmetry.

nodes.name: Definition and heuristic bound of I_3 (3.7)
nodes.statement: I_3 \coloneqq \bigI{ \tilde X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } = O(\eta k),
nodes.label: third-est-a

nodes.name: Endgame in the exactly independent case
nodes.statement: Suppose first for simplicity that the mutual informations in~\eqref{first-est-a},\ \eqref{second-est-a} and~\eqref{third-est-a} were zero rather than merely small. It follows that for any $s$ in the support of $X_1+X_2+ \tilde X_1+\tilde X_2$, the three random variables \begin{align} \nonumber T_1&= (X_1+X_2 |X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2=s),\\ \nonumber T_2&=(X_1+\tilde X_1 |X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2=s), \\ T_3&=(\tilde X_1+X_2 |X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2=s) \end{align} are pairwise independent. We also note that $T_1+T_2+T_3$ is constant (in fact it is identically zero). However, for any trio $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ of pairwise independent random variables such that $T_1+T_2+T_3$ is constant, a short calculation shows that \[\dist{T_1}{T_2} = \ent{T_3} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{T_1} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{T_2} \] and similarly for cyclic permutations, hence \begin{equation} \dist{T_1}{T_2} + \dist{T_1}{T_3} + \dist{T_2}{T_3} = 0 \end{equation} and so, taking $X'_1$ and $X'_2$ to be some pair of $T_1,T_2,T_3$, we have $\dist{X_1'}{X_2'} = 0$. This is a very strong conclusion, and with some further estimation, it allows us to establish~\eqref{d-opt}. (The choice of $X'_1,X'_2$ here is inspired, albeit rather indirectly, by a step in an argument of Katz and Koester~\cite{kk}.)
nodes.statement_short: If the three mutual informations vanish, $T_1,T_2,T_3$ are pairwise independent with constant sum, so their pairwise distances sum to zero.

nodes.name: The three conditioned sums T_1, T_2, T_3 (3.8)
nodes.statement: \nonumber T_1&= (X_1+X_2 |X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2=s),\\ \nonumber T_2&=(X_1+\tilde X_1 |X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2=s), \\ T_3&=(\tilde X_1+X_2 |X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2=s)
nodes.label: three-variables

nodes.name: Endgame via entropic Balog--Szemeredi--Gowers (plan)
nodes.statement: If the three variables in~\eqref{three-variables} are merely `almost pairwise independent', as in~\eqref{first-est-a} and~\eqref{second-est-a}, then things are less straightforward. Very roughly, sums of non-independent random variables are to sums of independent random variables as \emph{partial} sumsets $A+_E B$ along a bipartite graph $E$ are to full sumsets $A+B$. Hence, it is natural to apply a variant of the entropic Balog--Szemer\'edi--Gowers lemma due to the fourth author~\cite[Lemma 3.3]{tao-entropy} (reproduced as \Cref{lem-bsg} here) to pass from the `almost independent' variables $(T_1,T_2)$ as above, for which $\ent{T_1+T_2}-\tfrac12 \ent{T_1} - \tfrac12 \ent{T_2}$ is small (or even negative), to variables $X_1',X_2'$ with $\dist{X_1'}{X_2'} = O(\eta k)$. These variables $X'_1,X'_2$, which are given to us by \Cref{lem-bsg}, now establish~\eqref{d-opt}.
nodes.statement_short: For almost pairwise independent $T_i$, apply the entropic BSG lemma to obtain variables with distance $O(\eta k)$.

nodes.name: Form of the final choice of X'_1
nodes.statement: Examining the proof of \Cref{lem-bsg} carefully, the final choice of $X'_1$ that comes out of this argument is of the form \begin{equation} (X_1 + X_2 \,|\, \tilde X_1+ X_2 = t, X_1 + \tilde X_2 = s+t) \end{equation} or a related quantity obtained by permuting the variables, and similarly for $X'_2$ (using the same $s,t$ for both $X_1'$ and $X_2'$).
nodes.statement_short: The BSG step produces $X'_1$ of the form (3.10), a sum conditioned on two fibres.

nodes.name: Final choice from BSG (3.10)
nodes.statement: (X_1 + X_2 \,|\, \tilde X_1+ X_2 = t, X_1 + \tilde X_2 = s+t)
nodes.label: from-bsg

nodes.name: Doubling parameter K
nodes.statement: In this discussion is convenient to write $K \coloneqq e^k$.

nodes.name: Random subset of a subgroup
nodes.statement: Consider first the case in which $A_1=A_2=A$ and $A$ is a random subset of some subgroup $H \leqslant \mathbf{F}_2^n$ with density $K^{-1}$ in $H$. Then (almost surely) $\dist{X_1}{X_2} \approx k$. In this case the choice~\eqref{sum-2}, that is to say $X'_1 = X_1 + \tilde X_1$ and $X'_2 = X_2 + \tilde X_2$, immediately establishes~\eqref{d-opt}. Indeed both $X'_1$ and $X'_2$ are close to the uniform distribution $U_H$ on $H$, so $\dist{X'_1}{X'_2} \approx 0$ and $\dist{X'_i}{X_i}\approx k/2$ for $i=1,2$, and~\eqref{d-opt} follows, with room to spare, by the triangle inequality.
nodes.statement_short: For a random dense subset of a subgroup the sum choice (3.2) already gives (2.2).

nodes.name: Unions of independent cosets
nodes.statement: Consider next the case in which $A_1 = \bigcup_{i = 1}^{m} (x_i + H)$ and $A_2 = \bigcup_{i=1}^m (y_i+ H)$, where $H < \mathbf{F}_2^n$ is a subgroup and the $x_i+H$ and $y_i+H$ are linearly independent in $G/H$. Setting $m \coloneqq K$ gives $\dist{X_1}{X_2} \approx k$. In this case one can obtain~\eqref{d-opt} with the choice~\eqref{fiber-1}, that is to say $X'_1 = (X_1 | X_1 + \tilde X_2 = g)$ and $X'_2 = (X_2 | X_2 + \tilde X_1 = g')$ for any $g,g' \in A_1+A_2$. Indeed, $X'_1$ is the uniform distribution on $A_1 \cap (A_2 + g)$, which if $g \in x_i+y_j+H$ is exactly the coset $x_i+H$ of $H$ (by linear independence). Similarly, $X'_2$ is uniform on a coset $y_j'+H$, so $\dist{X'_1}{X'_2} \approx 0$ and again~\eqref{d-opt} follows. (Using the fibres in~\eqref{fiber-2} also gives a contradiction in this case, but the analysis is slightly more involved, since $A_1 \cap (A_1 + g)$ is typically a union of two cosets of $H$.)
nodes.statement_short: For unions of linearly independent cosets the fibre choice (3.3) gives (2.2).

nodes.name: Random subsets of unions of cosets (endgame needed)
nodes.statement: Here is a third example, a sort of combination of the previous two, for which the choices~\eqref{sum-1},~\eqref{sum-2},~\eqref{fiber-1} and~\eqref{fiber-2} all fail to work. Let $A_1',A_2'$ be (independent) random subsets of density $1/m$ of the sets $A_1,A_2$ from the previous example, where now $m = \sqrt{K}$. One may then check that $X_1 + \tilde X_1, X_2 + \tilde X_2$ resemble the uniform distribution on the union of $\approx K/2$ cosets of $H$, so $\dist{X'_1}{X'_2} \approx k - O(1)$ and we do not obtain~\eqref{d-opt} (if $k$ is large) with the choice~\eqref{sum-2}. The case of~\eqref{sum-1} is similar. On the other hand, the variables $(X_1 | X_1 + \tilde X_2 = g)$, $(X_2 | X_2 + \tilde X_1 = g')$ will be uniform on $A_1 \cap (A_2 + g)$ and $A_2 \cap (A_1+g')$ respectively, and such sets will typically (when non-empty) resemble random subsets of a coset of $H$, of density $1/m^2 \approx 1/K$. For these variables we also have $\dist{X'_1}{X'_2} \approx k$, and so we do not obtain~\eqref{d-opt} with the choice~\eqref{fiber-1}. The case of~\eqref{fiber-2} is broadly similar. We therefore proceed to the endgame and consider the three variables in~\eqref{three-variables}. Since $X_1+X_2$ is roughly uniform on $B \coloneqq \bigcup_{i,j} (x_i+y_j+H)$, a similar analysis to the second example shows that $(X_1+X_2 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2 = s)$ is roughly uniform on $B \cap (B+s)$, which is typically a union of four cosets of $H$, and similarly for $(\tilde X_1+X_2 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2 = s)$. Moreover, one can check that these two variables are `50\% independent' (in that knowing one of them narrows the choice of the other to two cosets of $H$). If we then apply \Cref{lem-bsg}, we find variables $X'_1$, $X'_2$ of the form given in~\eqref{from-bsg}. In other words, $X'_1$ is a sum of two variables of the form $(X_1 | X_1 + \tilde X_2 = a)$ and $(X_2 | X_2 + \tilde X_1 = b)$. Each will be uniform on a random subset of a coset of $H$, and adding them together will give something close to uniform on a coset of $H$. The case of $X'_2$ is similar, so we get $\dist{X'_1}{X'_2} \approx 0$ and~\eqref{d-opt} follows. (Again, permuting the variables may give slighly different conclusions.)
nodes.statement_short: Random sparse subsets of coset unions defeat all four choices; the endgame via BSG still works.

nodes.name: Discrete Gaussians over Z
nodes.statement: Finally, we consider a further example over $G = \mathbf{Z}$ instead of $\mathbf{F}_2^n$. Take $X_1,X_2$ to have a `discrete Gaussian' distribution $p(x) = C_0 e^{-x^2/2r^2}$ with some large `width' $r$ and a normalizing constant $C_0$. By~\cite[Theorem~1.13]{tao-entropy}, the distance $\dist{X_1}{X_2} \approx \frac12 \log 2$ is roughly minimal among random variables on $\mathbf{Z}$ with large entropy, and hence \Cref{de-prop} cannot hold over $\mathbf{Z}$ in the form stated. Concretely, one can show that sums $X_i+\tilde X_j$ as in~\eqref{sum-1},~\eqref{sum-2} are (roughly) discrete Gaussians of width $\sqrt2r$, and fibres $(X_i | X_i+\tilde X_j)$ as in~\eqref{fiber-1},~\eqref{fiber-2} are (shifted) discrete Gaussians of width about $r/\sqrt2$. Hence, all these have essentially the same value of $\dist{-}{-}$, and there is no way of `improving' these variables with any of the choices considered in \Cref{first,second}. One could also see directly that the conditional near-independence statements such as \[ \I{X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2} \approx 0 \] do indeed hold for discrete Gaussians. In the above one-dimensional example, the entropic doubling constant is bounded, and so this example does not, by itself, present a strong obstruction to the entire approach. However, by considering discrete gaussian examples in a high-dimensional lattice $\mathbf{Z}^d$, the entropic doubling constant is now close to $\frac{d}{2} \log 2$, which is unbounded, and all the moves considered previously do not significantly reduce this constant. Even though discrete Gaussians over $\mathbf{F}_2$ do not exist, this example places significant constraints on what we can hope to prove in general. In particular, it shows that the endgame argument must `see' the finite characteristic in an essential way.
nodes.statement_short: Discrete Gaussians on $\mathbf{Z}$ (or $\mathbf{Z}^d$) are not improved by any choice, so the endgame must use finite characteristic.

nodes.name: Contrapositive hypothesis: (X_1,X_2) minimises tau
nodes.statement: Thus, suppose henceforth that we have a pair $(X_1, X_2)$ of $G$-valued random variables with $\dist{X_1}{X_2} = k$ for some $k$, and suppose that \begin{equation} \tau[X'_1;X'_2] \geqslant \tau[X_1;X_2] \end{equation} for every pair of $G$-valued random variables $(X'_1, X'_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $d[X_1;X_2]=k$ and that no pair has smaller $\tau$.

nodes.name: No tau decrement (3.11)
nodes.statement: \tau[X'_1;X'_2] \geqslant \tau[X_1;X_2]
nodes.label: to-contradict'

nodes.name: Contradiction hypothesis in distance form (3.12)
nodes.statement: \dist{X'_1}{X'_2} \geqslant k - \costa{X'_1} - \costb{X'_2}.
nodes.label: to-contradict

nodes.name: First estimate
nodes.statement: Testing~\eqref{to-contradict} with the choices~\eqref{sum-1},~\eqref{fiber-1} will lead us to the conclusion that \begin{equation} I_1 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k \end{equation} (that is, a more precise version of~\eqref{first-est-a}).
conclusions: I_1 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k
also_stated_at: I_1 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k.
nodes.statement_short: Under the contradiction hypothesis, $I_1 \le 2\eta k$.

nodes.name: First estimate inequality (3.13)
nodes.statement: I_1 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k
nodes.label: first-est

nodes.name: Second estimate
nodes.statement: Testing~\eqref{to-contradict} with the choices~\eqref{sum-2},~\eqref{fiber-2} leads to \begin{equation} I_2 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k + \frac{2 \eta (2 \eta k - I_1)}{1 - \eta} \end{equation} (a more precise version of~\eqref{second-est-a}), and of course the same estimate holds for $I_3$, since in fact $I_2=I_3$.
conclusions: I_2 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k + \frac{2 \eta (2 \eta k - I_1)}{1 - \eta}
the same estimate holds for $I_3$
also_stated_at: I_2 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k + \frac{2 \eta (2 \eta k - I_1)}{1 - \eta}.
nodes.statement_short: Under the contradiction hypothesis, $I_2=I_3 \le 2\eta k + 2\eta(2\eta k-I_1)/(1-\eta)$.

nodes.name: Second estimate inequality (3.14)
nodes.statement: I_2 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k + \frac{2 \eta (2 \eta k - I_1)}{1 - \eta}
nodes.label: second-est

nodes.name: Conditioned contradiction hypothesis
nodes.statement: Note that~\eqref{to-contradict} implies a conditioned version of itself: for any random variables $(X_1',Y_1)$ and $(X_2',Y_2)$ we may apply~\eqref{to-contradict} with $X'_1, X'_2$ replaced by each of the conditioned random variables $(X'_1 | Y_1 = y_1) , (X'_2 | Y_2 = y_2)$, obtaining \begin{align*} & \dist{(X'_1 | Y_1 = y_1)}{(X'_2 | Y_2 = y_2)} \\ & \qquad\qquad\qquad \geqslant k \begin{aligned}[t] &- \costa{(X'_1 | Y_1 = y_1)} \\ &- \costb{(X'_2 | Y_2 = y_2)}. \end{aligned} \end{align*} Multiplying by $p_{Y_1}(y_1) p_{Y_2}(y_2)$ and summing, we have \begin{align} \nonumber \dist{X'_1 | Y_1}{X'_2 | Y_2} \geqslant k &- \costa{X'_1 | Y_1} \\ &- \costb{X'_2 | Y_2}. \end{align}
conclusions: \dist{X'_1 | Y_1}{X'_2 | Y_2} \geqslant k &- \costa{X'_1 | Y_1} \\ \label{to-contradict-avg} &- \costb{X'_2 | Y_2}.
nodes.statement_short: Averaging (3.12) over the conditioning values gives the same lower bound for conditional distances.

nodes.name: Conditioned contradiction hypothesis (3.15)
nodes.statement: \nonumber \dist{X'_1 | Y_1}{X'_2 | Y_2} \geqslant k &- \costa{X'_1 | Y_1} \\ &- \costb{X'_2 | Y_2}.
nodes.label: to-contradict-avg

nodes.name: Remarks on odd characteristic
nodes.statement: We will handle the case $p$ odd in our forthcoming paper~\cite{ggmt-pfr-odd}. All of the above steps go through, except for the final contradiction in the `endgame' where we used an argument specific to characteristic $2$. To get a contradiction in characteristic $p$, it is necessary to run a variant of the argument with a $p$-partite `distance' function $\operatorname{D}[X_1;\dots; X_p]$ replacing $\dist{X_1}{X_2}$ as the main term in the functional to be minimized. This introduces additional notational complexity: for instance we now have an array $(X_{ij})_{i,j \in \mathbf{F}_p}$ of random variables, and the fibring lemma must be generalized to this $p$-partite distance and applied $p-1$ times.
nodes.statement_short: Odd $p$ needs a $p$-partite distance and a generalized fibring lemma applied $p-1$ times.

nodes.name: Fibring lemma
nodes.statement: Let $\pi \colon H \to H'$ be a homomorphism between abelian groups and let $Z_1,Z_2$ be $H$-valued random variables. Then we have \[ \dist{Z_1}{Z_2} \geqslant \dist{\pi(Z_1)}{\pi(Z_2)} + \dist{Z_1|\pi(Z_1)}{Z_2 |\pi(Z_2)} \] where the notation is as in~\eqref{cond-dist-def}. Moreover, if $Z_1,Z_2$ are taken to be independent, then the difference between the two sides is \begin{equation} \bigI{ Z_1 - Z_2 : (\pi(Z_1), \pi(Z_2)) \; | \; \pi(Z_1 - Z_2)}. \end{equation}
assumptions: $\pi \colon H \to H'$ be a homomorphism between abelian groups
conclusions: \dist{Z_1}{Z_2} \geqslant \dist{\pi(Z_1)}{\pi(Z_2)} + \dist{Z_1|\pi(Z_1)}{Z_2 |\pi(Z_2)}
the difference between the two sides is \begin{equation} \label{mut-info-cond} \bigI{ Z_1 - Z_2 : (\pi(Z_1), \pi(Z_2)) \; | \; \pi(Z_1 - Z_2)}. \end{equation}
\dist{Z_1}{Z_2} \geqslant \dist{\pi(Z_1)}{\pi(Z_2)} + \dist{Z_1|\pi(Z_1)}{Z_2 |\pi(Z_2)}
the difference between the two sides is \begin{equation} \label{mut-info-cond} \bigI{ Z_1 - Z_2 : (\pi(Z_1), \pi(Z_2)) \; | \; \pi(Z_1 - Z_2)}. \end{equation}

nodes.statement_short: Ruzsa distance splits under a homomorphism into image distance plus fibre distance, with the defect a conditional mutual information.
nodes.label: projections-1

nodes.name: Proof of the fibring lemma
nodes.statement: Let $Z_1,Z_2$ be independent throughout. We have \begin{align*} & \bigdist{Z_1 |\pi(Z_1)}{ Z_2 |\pi(Z_2)} \\ & = \bigH{ Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_2)} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{Z_1 | \pi(Z_1)} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Z_2 | \pi(Z_2)} \\ & \leqslant \bigH{ Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1-Z_2)} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{Z_1 | \pi(Z_1)} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Z_2 | \pi(Z_2)} \\ & = \dist{Z_1}{Z_2} - \dist{\pi(Z_1)}{\pi(Z_2)}. \end{align*} In the middle step, we used submodularity of entropy, and in the last step we used the fact that \[ \bigH{ Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1-Z_2)} = \ent{Z_1 - Z_2} - \ent{\pi(Z_1-Z_2)}\] (since $Z_1 - Z_2$ determines $\pi(Z_1 - Z_2)$) and that \[ \ent{Z_i| \pi(Z_i)} = \ent{Z_i} - \ent{\pi(Z_i)}\] (since $Z_i$ determines $\pi(Z_i)$). This gives the claimed inequality. The difference between the two sides is precisely \[ \bigH{Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1 - Z_2)} - \bigH{Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_2)}.\] To rewrite this in terms of (conditional) mutual information, we use the identity \[ \ent{A|B} - \ent{A | B,C} = \I{A : C | B},\] taking $A \coloneqq Z_1 - Z_2$, $B \coloneqq \pi(Z_1 - Z_2)$ and $C \coloneqq (\pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_{2}))$, and noting that in this case $\ent{A | B,C} = \ent{A | C}$ since $C$ uniquely determines $B$. This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Submodularity of entropy plus chain-rule identities; the defect is rewritten as a conditional mutual information.

nodes.name: Main calculation
nodes.statement: Let $Z_1,Z_2$ be independent throughout. We have \begin{align*} & \bigdist{Z_1 |\pi(Z_1)}{ Z_2 |\pi(Z_2)} \\ & = \bigH{ Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_2)} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{Z_1 | \pi(Z_1)} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Z_2 | \pi(Z_2)} \\ & \leqslant \bigH{ Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1-Z_2)} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{Z_1 | \pi(Z_1)} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Z_2 | \pi(Z_2)} \\ & = \dist{Z_1}{Z_2} - \dist{\pi(Z_1)}{\pi(Z_2)}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand the fibre distance and bound it via submodularity.

nodes.name: Justification
nodes.statement: In the middle step, we used submodularity of entropy, and in the last step we used the fact that \[ \bigH{ Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1-Z_2)} = \ent{Z_1 - Z_2} - \ent{\pi(Z_1-Z_2)}\] (since $Z_1 - Z_2$ determines $\pi(Z_1 - Z_2)$) and that \[ \ent{Z_i| \pi(Z_i)} = \ent{Z_i} - \ent{\pi(Z_i)}\] (since $Z_i$ determines $\pi(Z_i)$). This gives the claimed inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Justify the steps by submodularity and determinism of $\pi$.

nodes.name: Identify the gap
nodes.statement: The difference between the two sides is precisely \[ \bigH{Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1 - Z_2)} - \bigH{Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_2)}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Identify the gap as a difference of conditional entropies.

nodes.name: Mutual information form
nodes.statement: To rewrite this in terms of (conditional) mutual information, we use the identity \[ \ent{A|B} - \ent{A | B,C} = \I{A : C | B},\] taking $A \coloneqq Z_1 - Z_2$, $B \coloneqq \pi(Z_1 - Z_2)$ and $C \coloneqq (\pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_{2}))$, and noting that in this case $\ent{A | B,C} = \ent{A | C}$ since $C$ uniquely determines $B$. This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the gap as conditional mutual information.

nodes.name: Fibring identity for four independent variables
nodes.statement: Let $Y_1,Y_2,Y_3$ and $Y_4$ be independent random variables taking values in some abelian group $G$. Then \begin{align*} \nonumber & \dist{Y_1-Y_3}{Y_2-Y_4} + \bigdist{Y_1|Y_1-Y_3}{Y_2|Y_2-Y_4} \\ &\qquad + \bigI{ Y_1-Y_2 : Y_2 - Y_4 | Y_1-Y_2-Y_3+Y_4 } = \dist{Y_1}{Y_2} + \dist{Y_3}{Y_4}. \end{align*}
assumptions: $Y_1,Y_2,Y_3$ and $Y_4$ be independent random variables taking values in some abelian group $G$
nodes.statement_short: For four independent variables, distance of differences plus fibre distance plus a mutual information equals $d[Y_1;Y_2]+d[Y_3;Y_4]$.
nodes.label: cor-fibre

nodes.name: Proof of the four-variable fibring identity
nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{projections-1} with $H \coloneqq G \times G$, $H' \coloneqq G$, $\pi$ the subtraction homomorphism $\pi(x,y) \coloneqq x-y$, and with the random variables $Z_1 \coloneqq (Y_1,Y_3)$ and $Z_2 \coloneqq (Y_2,Y_4)$. Then by independence we easily calculate \[ \dist{Z_1}{Z_2} = \dist{Y_1}{Y_2} + \dist{Y_3}{Y_4} \] while by definition \[ \dist{\pi(Z_1)}{\pi(Z_2)} = \dist{Y_1-Y_3}{Y_2-Y_4}. \] Furthermore, \[ \dist{Z_1|\pi(Z_1)}{Z_2|\pi(Z_2)} = \dist{Y_1|Y_1-Y_3}{Y_2|Y_2-Y_4}, \] since $Z_1=(Y_1,Y_3)$ and $Y_1$ are linked by an invertible affine transformation once $\pi(Z_1)=Y_1-Y_3$ is fixed, and similarly for $Z_2$ and $Y_2$. Finally, we have \begin{align*} &\bigI{Z_1 - Z_2 : (\pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_2)) \,|\, \pi(Z_1) + \pi(Z_2)} \\ &\ = \bigI{(Y_1-Y_2, Y_3-Y_4) : (Y_1-Y_3, Y_2-Y_4) \,|\, Y_1-Y_2-Y_3+Y_4} \\ &\ = \bigI{Y_1-Y_2 : Y_2-Y_4 \,|\, Y_1-Y_2-Y_3+Y_4} \end{align*} where in the last line we used the fact that $(Y_1-Y_2, Y_1-Y_2-Y_3+Y_4)$ uniquely determine $Y_3-Y_4$ and similarly $(Y_2-Y_4, Y_1-Y_2-Y_3+Y_4)$ uniquely determine $Y_1-Y_3$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the fibring lemma to $G\times G \to G$, $(x,y)\mapsto x-y$, with $Z_1=(Y_1,Y_3)$, $Z_2=(Y_2,Y_4)$.

nodes.name: Set up the fibring lemma
nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{projections-1} with $H \coloneqq G \times G$, $H' \coloneqq G$, $\pi$ the subtraction homomorphism $\pi(x,y) \coloneqq x-y$, and with the random variables $Z_1 \coloneqq (Y_1,Y_3)$ and $Z_2 \coloneqq (Y_2,Y_4)$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the fibring lemma to the subtraction map.

nodes.name: Compute distances
nodes.statement: Then by independence we easily calculate \[ \dist{Z_1}{Z_2} = \dist{Y_1}{Y_2} + \dist{Y_3}{Y_4} \] while by definition \[ \dist{\pi(Z_1)}{\pi(Z_2)} = \dist{Y_1-Y_3}{Y_2-Y_4}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Compute the two distance terms.

nodes.name: Fibre term
nodes.statement: Furthermore, \[ \dist{Z_1|\pi(Z_1)}{Z_2|\pi(Z_2)} = \dist{Y_1|Y_1-Y_3}{Y_2|Y_2-Y_4}, \] since $Z_1=(Y_1,Y_3)$ and $Y_1$ are linked by an invertible affine transformation once $\pi(Z_1)=Y_1-Y_3$ is fixed, and similarly for $Z_2$ and $Y_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the fibre distance.

nodes.name: Mutual information term
nodes.statement: Finally, we have \begin{align*} &\bigI{Z_1 - Z_2 : (\pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_2)) \,|\, \pi(Z_1) + \pi(Z_2)} \\ &\ = \bigI{(Y_1-Y_2, Y_3-Y_4) : (Y_1-Y_3, Y_2-Y_4) \,|\, Y_1-Y_2-Y_3+Y_4} \\ &\ = \bigI{Y_1-Y_2 : Y_2-Y_4 \,|\, Y_1-Y_2-Y_3+Y_4} \end{align*} where in the last line we used the fact that $(Y_1-Y_2, Y_1-Y_2-Y_3+Y_4)$ uniquely determine $Y_3-Y_4$ and similarly $(Y_2-Y_4, Y_1-Y_2-Y_3+Y_4)$ uniquely determine $Y_1-Y_3$.
nodes.statement_short: Simplify the mutual information term.

nodes.name: Characteristic 2 sign convention
nodes.statement: Of course, in our main characteristic $2$ setting, the minus signs in \Cref{projections-1,cor-fibre} may be replaced with plus signs.
nodes.label: rem:char2

nodes.name: Proof of the first estimate
nodes.statement_short: Apply the four-variable fibring identity to $(X_1,X_2,\tilde X_2,\tilde X_1)$ and the contradiction hypothesis; bound the penalty terms by Lemma 5.2.

nodes.name: Conditioning bound for Ruzsa distance
nodes.statement: Suppose that $(X, Z)$ and $(Y, W)$ are random variables, where $X, Y$ take values in some abelian group. Then \[ \dist{X | Z}{Y | W} \leqslant \dist{X}{Y} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{X : Z} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{Y : W}.\]
assumptions: $(X, Z)$ and $(Y, W)$ are random variables, where $X, Y$ take values in some abelian group
conclusions: \dist{X | Z}{Y | W} \leqslant \dist{X}{Y} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{X : Z} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{Y : W}.
nodes.statement_short: Conditioning increases Ruzsa distance by at most half the mutual informations.
nodes.label: cond-dist-fact

nodes.name: Proof of the conditioning bound
nodes.statement: The definition of conditional distance is given in~\eqref{cond-dist-def}. Using the alternative expression~\eqref{cond-dist-alt}, if $(X',Z'), (Y',W')$ are independent copies of the variables $(X,Z)$, $(Y,W)$, we have \begin{align*} \dist{X | Z}{Y | W} &= \ent{X'-Y'|Z',W'} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X'|Z'} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Y'|W'} \\ &\leqslant \ent{X'-Y'}- \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X'|Z'} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Y'|W'} \\ &= \dist{X'}{Y'} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{X' : Z'} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{Y' : W'}. \end{align*} Here, in the middle step we used~\eqref{cond-dec}, and in the last step we used the definitions of $\dist{-}{-}$ and $\I{-}$.
nodes.statement_short: Use the alternative expression for conditional distance and that conditioning reduces entropy.

nodes.name: Recall definition
nodes.statement: The definition of conditional distance is given in~\eqref{cond-dist-def}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the definition of conditional distance.

nodes.name: Calculation
nodes.statement: Using the alternative expression~\eqref{cond-dist-alt}, if $(X',Z'), (Y',W')$ are independent copies of the variables $(X,Z)$, $(Y,W)$, we have \begin{align*} \dist{X | Z}{Y | W} &= \ent{X'-Y'|Z',W'} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X'|Z'} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Y'|W'} \\ &\leqslant \ent{X'-Y'}- \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X'|Z'} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Y'|W'} \\ &= \dist{X'}{Y'} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{X' : Z'} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{Y' : W'}. \end{align*} Here, in the middle step we used~\eqref{cond-dec}, and in the last step we used the definitions of $\dist{-}{-}$ and $\I{-}$.
nodes.statement_short: Expand via (A.15), drop conditioning by (A.5), and recognise $d$ and $I$.

nodes.name: Distance change under sums and fibres
nodes.statement: Let $X, Y, Z$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group, and with $Y, Z$ independent. Then we have\footnote{We thank Floris van Doorn for noting a sign discrepancy in a previous version of this statement, which was uncovered as part of the effort to formalize the results of this paper in {\tt Lean 4}.} \begin{align}\nonumber \dist{X}{Y - Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} (\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Y}) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y} \end{align} and \begin{align}\nonumber \dist{X}{Y|Y-Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \bigl(\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Z}\bigr) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z}. \end{align}
assumptions: $X, Y, Z$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group
conclusions: \dist{X}{Y - Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} (\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Y}) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y}
\dist{X}{Y|Y-Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \bigl(\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Z}\bigr) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z}.
nodes.statement_short: Replacing $Y$ by $Y-Z$ or by $(Y|Y-Z)$ raises the distance to any $X$ by at most about $\frac12 d[Y;Z]$.
nodes.label: first-useful

nodes.name: Sum bound (5.5)
nodes.statement: \nonumber \dist{X}{Y - Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} (\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Y}) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y}
nodes.label: lem51-a

nodes.name: Fibre bound (5.6)
nodes.statement: \nonumber \dist{X}{Y|Y-Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \bigl(\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Z}\bigr) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z}.
nodes.label: ruzsa-3

nodes.name: Proof of the distance-change lemma
nodes.statement: We first prove~\eqref{lem51-a}. We may assume (taking an independent copy) that $X$ is independent of $Y, Z$. Then we have \begin{align*} \dist{X}{Y-Z} & - \dist{X}{Y} \\ & = \ent{X - Y + Z} - \ent{X-Y} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Y - Z} + \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{Y}.\end{align*} Combining this with~\eqref{kv-2} (applied with $Y$ replaced by $-Y$) gives the required bound. The second form of the result is immediate from the definition of $\dist{Y}{Z}$, since $Y, Z$ are independent. Turning to~\eqref{ruzsa-3}, we have \begin{align*} \I{Y : Y-Z} & = \ent{Y} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y, Y - Z} \\ & = \ent{Y} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y, Z} = \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Z},\end{align*} and so~\eqref{ruzsa-3} is a consequence of~\Cref{cond-dist-fact}. Once again the second form of the result is immediate from the definition of $\dist{Y}{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: (5.5) from Madiman's inequality; (5.6) from the conditioning bound with $I[Y:Y-Z]=H[Y-Z]-H[Z]$.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: We first prove~\eqref{lem51-a}. We may assume (taking an independent copy) that $X$ is independent of $Y, Z$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $X$ independent of $Y,Z$.

nodes.name: Expand
nodes.statement: Then we have \begin{align*} \dist{X}{Y-Z} & - \dist{X}{Y} \\ & = \ent{X - Y + Z} - \ent{X-Y} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Y - Z} + \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{Y}.\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand the distance difference into entropies.

nodes.name: Apply Madiman
nodes.statement: Combining this with~\eqref{kv-2} (applied with $Y$ replaced by $-Y$) gives the required bound. The second form of the result is immediate from the definition of $\dist{Y}{Z}$, since $Y, Z$ are independent.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Madiman's inequality with $-Y$.

nodes.name: Fibre bound
nodes.statement: Turning to~\eqref{ruzsa-3}, we have \begin{align*} \I{Y : Y-Z} & = \ent{Y} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y, Y - Z} \\ & = \ent{Y} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y, Z} = \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Z},\end{align*} and so~\eqref{ruzsa-3} is a consequence of~\Cref{cond-dist-fact}. Once again the second form of the result is immediate from the definition of $\dist{Y}{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute $I[Y:Y-Z]$ and apply Lemma 5.1.

nodes.name: Fibring identity for the first choice (5.1)
nodes.statement: \nonumber &\dist{X_1+\tilde X_2}{X_2+\tilde X_1} + \bigdist{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1} \\ &\quad + \bigI{ X_1+ X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 \,|\, X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2 } = 2k,
nodes.label: second-main

nodes.name: Conditioned hypothesis for fibres (5.2)
nodes.statement: \nonumber & \dist{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1} \\ \nonumber & \qquad\quad \geqslant k - \costa{X_1 | X_1 + \tilde X_2} \\ & \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad - \costb{X_2 | X_2 + \tilde X_1}.
nodes.label: second-tc2

nodes.name: Sufficient penalty bound (5.3)
nodes.statement: \nonumber &(\dist{X_1^0}{X_1+\tilde X_2}-\dist{X_1^0}{X_1})+ (\dist{X_2^0}{X_2+\tilde X_1}-\dist{X_2^0}{X_2})\\ &\qquad \qquad +(\dist{X_1^0}{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2}-\dist{X_1^0}{X_1}) \nonumber \\ & \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad +(\dist{X_2^0}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1}-\dist{X_2^0}{X_2}) \leqslant 2k.
nodes.label: suff-for-first-est

nodes.name: Fibre penalty bound for X_1 (5.7)
nodes.statement: \dist{X_1^0}{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X_1^0}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_1} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_2}
nodes.label: second-dist1

nodes.name: Fibre penalty bound for X_2 (5.8)
nodes.statement: \dist{X_2^0}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X_2^0}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2}k + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_2} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_1}.
nodes.label: second-dist2

nodes.name: Entropy bound for S (5.9)
nodes.statement: \bigH{X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_1}+\tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_2} + (2 + \eta) k - I_1.
nodes.label: HS-bound

nodes.name: Recall the setting
nodes.statement: Recall that in this and subsequent sections we are working on the assumption that~\eqref{to-contradict} and its conditioned variant~\eqref{to-contradict-avg} hold, aiming to prove that $k = 0$ and hence conclude (the contrapositive of) Proposition~\ref{de-prop}. Recall also that $X_1, X_2, \tilde X_1, \tilde X_2$ are independent random variables, with $X_1,\tilde X_1$ copies of $X_1$ and $X_2,\tilde X_2$ copies of $X_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the contradiction hypothesis and the independent copies.

nodes.name: Target
nodes.statement: In this section we establish the upper bound~\eqref{first-est}, which was that \[ I_1 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k. \]
nodes.statement_short: State the target bound (3.13).

nodes.name: Fibring identity
nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{cor-fibre} (and Remark \ref{rem:char2}) with the choice \[ (Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4) \coloneqq (X_1, X_2, \tilde X_2, \tilde X_1). \] It gives \begin{align} \nonumber &\dist{X_1+\tilde X_2}{X_2+\tilde X_1} + \bigdist{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1} \\ &\quad + \bigI{ X_1+ X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 \,|\, X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2 } = 2k, \end{align} since $\dist{X_1}{X_2} = k$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the fibring identity to $(X_1,X_2,\tilde X_2,\tilde X_1)$.

nodes.name: Use the hypothesis
nodes.statement: Applying~\eqref{to-contradict},~\eqref{to-contradict-avg}, we have \begin{align*} \dist{X_1+\tilde X_2}{X_2+\tilde X_1} \geqslant k &- \costa{X_1+\tilde X_2} \\& \qquad- \costb{X_2+\tilde X_1} \end{align*} and \begin{align} \nonumber & \dist{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1} \\ \nonumber & \qquad\quad \geqslant k - \costa{X_1 | X_1 + \tilde X_2} \\ & \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad - \costb{X_2 | X_2 + \tilde X_1}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound the two distances by the contradiction hypothesis.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: It therefore suffices to prove that \begin{align} \nonumber &(\dist{X_1^0}{X_1+\tilde X_2}-\dist{X_1^0}{X_1})+ (\dist{X_2^0}{X_2+\tilde X_1}-\dist{X_2^0}{X_2})\\ &\qquad \qquad +(\dist{X_1^0}{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2}-\dist{X_1^0}{X_1}) \nonumber \\ & \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad +(\dist{X_2^0}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1}-\dist{X_2^0}{X_2}) \leqslant 2k. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to bounding the penalty terms by $2k$.

nodes.name: Auxiliary lemmas
nodes.statement: We pause to state some lemmas which we will use for bounding a number of similar expressions, both here and in the next two sections. The first is a bound relating conditioned and unconditioned variants of the Ruzsa distance. \begin{lemma} Suppose that $(X, Z)$ and $(Y, W)$ are random variables, where $X, Y$ take values in some abelian group. Then \[ \dist{X | Z}{Y | W} \leqslant \dist{X}{Y} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{X : Z} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{Y : W}.\] \end{lemma} \begin{proof} The definition of conditional distance is given in~\eqref{cond-dist-def}. Using the alternative expression~\eqref{cond-dist-alt}, if $(X',Z'), (Y',W')$ are independent copies of the variables $(X,Z)$, $(Y,W)$, we have \begin{align*} \dist{X | Z}{Y | W} &= \ent{X'-Y'|Z',W'} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X'|Z'} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Y'|W'} \\ &\leqslant \ent{X'-Y'}- \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X'|Z'} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Y'|W'} \\ &= \dist{X'}{Y'} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{X' : Z'} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{Y' : W'}. \end{align*} Here, in the middle step we used~\eqref{cond-dec}, and in the last step we used the definitions of $\dist{-}{-}$ and $\I{-}$. \end{proof} In the proof of the next lemma we will use the fact that, for any independent random variables $X, Y, Z$ taking values in an abelian group, we have the inequality \begin{equation} \ent{X + Y + Z} - \ent{X + Y} \leqslant \ent{Y+Z} - \ent{Y}. \end{equation} This is a result of Madiman~\cite[Theorem I]{madiman}, and is a more general form of an inequality of Kaimanovich and Vershik~\cite[Proposition 1.3]{kv}. It can be viewed as an entropy analogue of an inequality of Pl\"unnecke~\cite{plunnecke}. For the convenience of the reader, we give the proof in \Cref{entropy-app}. \begin{lemma} Let $X, Y, Z$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group, and with $Y, Z$ independent. Then we have\footnote{We thank Floris van Doorn for noting a sign discrepancy in a previous version of this statement, which was uncovered as part of the effort to formalize the results of this paper in {\tt Lean 4}.} \begin{align}\nonumber \dist{X}{Y - Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} (\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Y}) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y} \end{align} and \begin{align}\nonumber \dist{X}{Y|Y-Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \bigl(\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Z}\bigr) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z}. \end{align} \end{lemma} \begin{proof} We first prove~\eqref{lem51-a}. We may assume (taking an independent copy) that $X$ is independent of $Y, Z$. Then we have \begin{align*} \dist{X}{Y-Z} & - \dist{X}{Y} \\ & = \ent{X - Y + Z} - \ent{X-Y} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Y - Z} + \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{Y}.\end{align*} Combining this with~\eqref{kv-2} (applied with $Y$ replaced by $-Y$) gives the required bound. The second form of the result is immediate from the definition of $\dist{Y}{Z}$, since $Y, Z$ are independent. Turning to~\eqref{ruzsa-3}, we have \begin{align*} \I{Y : Y-Z} & = \ent{Y} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y, Y - Z} \\ & = \ent{Y} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y, Z} = \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Z},\end{align*} and so~\eqref{ruzsa-3} is a consequence of~\Cref{cond-dist-fact}. Once again the second form of the result is immediate from the definition of $\dist{Y}{Z}$. \end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Auxiliary Lemmas 5.1 and 5.2 with Madiman's inequality.

nodes.name: Bound penalties
nodes.statement: We return to our main task of establishing~\eqref{suff-for-first-est}, and hence~\eqref{first-est}. As usual, in the main setting $G=\mathbf{F}_2^n$ we may replace all minus signs with plus signs in the statement of \Cref{first-useful}. Hence by \Cref{first-useful} (and recalling that $k$ is defined to be $\dist{X_1}{X_2}$) we have \[ \dist{X^0_1}{X_1+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_2} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_1},\] \[ \dist{X^0_2}{X_2+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_1} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_2},\] \begin{equation} \dist{X_1^0}{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X_1^0}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_1} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_2} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \dist{X_2^0}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X_2^0}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2}k + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_2} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_1}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.2 bounds each of the four penalty terms.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Adding all these inequalities, we obtain~\eqref{suff-for-first-est}.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the four bounds.

nodes.name: Bound on H[S]
nodes.statement: For use in the next two sections, we note that subtracting~\eqref{second-tc2} from~\eqref{second-main}, and combining the resulting inequality with~\eqref{second-dist1} and~\eqref{second-dist2} gives the bound \[ \dist{X_1+\tilde X_2}{X_2+\tilde X_1} \leqslant (1 + \eta) k - I_1, \] which is equivalent to \begin{equation} \bigH{X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_1}+\tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_2} + (2 + \eta) k - I_1. \end{equation} One could also bound the left-hand side using~\eqref{kv-2} (twice), but by making use of our hypothesis~\eqref{to-contradict-avg} as above we obtain a slightly better constant.
nodes.statement_short: Derive the entropy bound (5.9) for later use.

nodes.name: Proof of the second estimate
nodes.statement: In this section we establish the upper bound~\eqref{second-est}, which was \[ I_2 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k + \frac{2 \eta (2 \eta k - I_1)}{1 - \eta}. \] We apply \Cref{cor-fibre} (and Remark \ref{rem:char2}), but now with the choice \[ (Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4) \coloneqq (X_2, X_1, \tilde X_2, \tilde X_1). \] Now \Cref{cor-fibre} can be rewritten as \begin{align*} &\dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} + \bigdist{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} \\ &\quad + \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 \,|\, X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } = 2k, \end{align*} recalling once again that $k \coloneqq \dist{X_1}{X_2}$. From~\eqref{to-contradict} and~\eqref{to-contradict-avg} as before, one has \begin{align} \nonumber \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k &- \costa{X_1+\tilde X_1} \\ &- \costb{X_2+\tilde X_2} \end{align} and \begin{align*} \dist{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k &- \costa{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1} \\& - \costb{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} . \end{align*} Now \Cref{first-useful} gives \begin{equation} \dist{X^0_1}{X_1+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_1}{X_1},\end{equation} \begin{equation} \dist{X^0_2}{X_2+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_2}{X_2}, \end{equation} \[ \dist{X^0_1}{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_1}{X_1}, \] and \[ \dist{X^0_2}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_2}{X_2}. \] Combining all these inequalities and cancelling terms, we obtain \begin{equation} \I{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant \eta ( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} ). \end{equation} One could bound the right-hand side by $4\eta k$ using the Ruzsa triangle inequality, but a more efficient approach is as follows. First, by combining~\eqref{1122},~\eqref{1122a} and~\eqref{1122b}, we obtain \begin{equation} \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k - \frac{\eta}{2} ( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} ). \end{equation} We may also expand \begin{align*} & \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \\ &= \ent{ X_1+\tilde X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_2} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_1+\tilde X_1} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_2+\tilde X_2} \\ &= \ent{ X_1+\tilde X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_2} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_1} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_2} \\ & \qquad\qquad\qquad - \tfrac{1}{2} \left( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \right), \end{align*} and hence by~\eqref{HS-bound} \[ \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \leqslant (2+\eta) k - \tfrac{1}{2} \left( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \right) - I_1. \] Combining this bound with~\eqref{d12} we obtain \begin{equation} \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \leqslant 2 k + \frac{2(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}. \end{equation} Therefore by~\eqref{combined} we have the desired bound \[ \I{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k + \frac{2\eta(2\eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Fibring identity with $(X_2,X_1,\tilde X_2,\tilde X_1)$ and Lemma 5.2 bound $I_2$ by $\eta(d[X_1;X_1]+d[X_2;X_2])$; (5.9) controls the self-distances.

nodes.name: Hypothesis for sums (6.1)
nodes.statement: \nonumber \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k &- \costa{X_1+\tilde X_1} \\ &- \costb{X_2+\tilde X_2}

nodes.name: Sum penalty for X_1 (6.2)
nodes.statement: \dist{X^0_1}{X_1+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_1}{X_1},
nodes.label: 1122a

nodes.name: Sum penalty for X_2 (6.3)
nodes.statement: \dist{X^0_2}{X_2+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_2}{X_2},
nodes.label: 1122b

nodes.name: Combined bound on I_2 (6.4)
nodes.statement: \I{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant \eta ( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} ).
nodes.label: combined

nodes.name: Lower bound for sum distance (6.5)
nodes.statement: \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k - \frac{\eta}{2} ( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} ).
nodes.label: d12

nodes.name: Self-distance bound (6.6)
nodes.statement: \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \leqslant 2 k + \frac{2(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}.
nodes.label: x12

nodes.name: Target
nodes.statement: In this section we establish the upper bound~\eqref{second-est}, which was \[ I_2 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k + \frac{2 \eta (2 \eta k - I_1)}{1 - \eta}. \]
nodes.statement_short: State the target bound (3.14).

nodes.name: Fibring identity
nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{cor-fibre} (and Remark \ref{rem:char2}), but now with the choice \[ (Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4) \coloneqq (X_2, X_1, \tilde X_2, \tilde X_1). \] Now \Cref{cor-fibre} can be rewritten as \begin{align*} &\dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} + \bigdist{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} \\ &\quad + \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 \,|\, X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } = 2k, \end{align*} recalling once again that $k \coloneqq \dist{X_1}{X_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fibring identity for $(X_2,X_1,\tilde X_2,\tilde X_1)$.

nodes.name: Use the hypothesis
nodes.statement: From~\eqref{to-contradict} and~\eqref{to-contradict-avg} as before, one has \begin{align} \nonumber \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k &- \costa{X_1+\tilde X_1} \\ &- \costb{X_2+\tilde X_2} \end{align} and \begin{align*} \dist{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k &- \costa{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1} \\& - \costb{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound the two distances by the hypothesis.

nodes.name: Bound penalties
nodes.statement: Now \Cref{first-useful} gives \begin{equation} \dist{X^0_1}{X_1+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_1}{X_1},\end{equation} \begin{equation} \dist{X^0_2}{X_2+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_2}{X_2}, \end{equation} \[ \dist{X^0_1}{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_1}{X_1}, \] and \[ \dist{X^0_2}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_2}{X_2}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.2 bounds the penalty terms by self-distances.

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combining all these inequalities and cancelling terms, we obtain \begin{equation} \I{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant \eta ( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} ). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lower bound
nodes.statement: One could bound the right-hand side by $4\eta k$ using the Ruzsa triangle inequality, but a more efficient approach is as follows. First, by combining~\eqref{1122},~\eqref{1122a} and~\eqref{1122b}, we obtain \begin{equation} \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k - \frac{\eta}{2} ( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} ). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound (6.5) for the sum distance.

nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement: We may also expand \begin{align*} & \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \\ &= \ent{ X_1+\tilde X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_2} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_1+\tilde X_1} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_2+\tilde X_2} \\ &= \ent{ X_1+\tilde X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_2} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_1} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_2} \\ & \qquad\qquad\qquad - \tfrac{1}{2} \left( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \right), \end{align*} and hence by~\eqref{HS-bound} \[ \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \leqslant (2+\eta) k - \tfrac{1}{2} \left( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \right) - I_1. \]
nodes.statement_short: Expand the sum distance and use (5.9) for an upper bound.

nodes.name: Self-distance bound
nodes.statement: Combining this bound with~\eqref{d12} we obtain \begin{equation} \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \leqslant 2 k + \frac{2(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the self-distances (6.6).

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Therefore by~\eqref{combined} we have the desired bound \[ \I{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k + \frac{2\eta(2\eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Insert (6.6) into (6.4).

nodes.name: Proof of the entropy decrement proposition (endgame)
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 7.2 to the conditioned triple $(U,V,W\mid S)$ with $U+V+W=0$; the estimates (7.2), (7.3) give $k \le (8\eta+\eta^2)k$, so $k=0$. The key step is the characteristic-2 identity $U+V+W=0$.

nodes.name: Distance change under a conditioned sum
nodes.statement: Let $X, Y, Z, Z'$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group, and with $Y, Z, Z'$ independent. Then we have \begin{align}\nonumber & \dist{X}{Y - Z | Y - Z - Z'} - \dist{X}{Y} \\ & \qquad \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} ( \ent{Y - Z - Z'} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y} - \ent{Z'}). \end{align}
assumptions: $X, Y, Z, Z'$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group
conclusions: & \dist{X}{Y - Z | Y - Z - Z'} - \dist{X}{Y} \\ & \qquad \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} ( \ent{Y - Z - Z'} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y} - \ent{Z'}).
nodes.statement_short: Bound on how much $d[X;\cdot]$ grows when $Y$ is replaced by $Y-Z$ conditioned on $Y-Z-Z'$.
nodes.label: second-useful

nodes.name: Conditioned sum bound (7.1)
nodes.statement: \nonumber & \dist{X}{Y - Z | Y - Z - Z'} - \dist{X}{Y} \\ & \qquad \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} ( \ent{Y - Z - Z'} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y} - \ent{Z'}).

nodes.name: Proof of the conditioned-sum bound
nodes.statement: By~\eqref{ruzsa-3} (with a change of variables) we have \[ \dist{X}{Y - Z | Y - Z - Z'} - \dist{X}{Y - Z} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2}( \ent{Y - Z - Z'} - \ent{Z'}).\] Adding this to~\eqref{lem51-a} gives the result.
nodes.statement_short: Add the fibre bound (5.6) after a change of variables to the sum bound (5.5).

nodes.name: Sum of the three mutual informations (7.2)
nodes.statement: \nonumber \I{U : V \, | \, S} + \I{V : W \, | \,S} &+ \I{W : U \, | \, S}\\ \nonumber &\leqslant I_1+4\eta k+ \frac{4\eta(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}\\ &= 6 \eta k - \frac{1 - 5 \eta}{1-\eta} (2 \eta k - I_1).
nodes.label: uvw-s

nodes.name: Total penalty bound (7.3)
nodes.statement: \nonumber \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A\in\{U,V,W\}} \big(\dist{X^0_i}{A|S} & - \dist{X^0_i}{X_i}\big) \\ &\leqslant 3\ent{S} - \tfrac{3}{2} \ent{X_1} - \tfrac{3}{2}\ent{X_2} \nonumber \\ &\leqslant (6 - 3\eta) k + 3(2 \eta k - I_1).
nodes.label: total-dist

nodes.name: Abstract endgame lemma
nodes.statement: Let $G=\mathbf{F}_2^n$ and let $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ be a $G^3$-valued random variable such that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically. Set \begin{equation} \delta \coloneqq \sum_{1 \leqslant i < j \leqslant 3} \I{T_i;T_j}. \end{equation} Then there exist random variables $T'_1, T'_2$ such that \begin{align*} \dist{T'_1}{T'_2} + & \eta (\dist{X_1^0}{T'_1} - \dist{X_1^0}{X_1}) + \eta(\dist{X_2^0}{T'_2} - \dist{X_2^0}{X_2}) \\ & \leqslant \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j = 1}^3 (\dist{X^0_i}{T_j} - \dist{X^0_i}{X_i}) \biggr). \end{align*}
assumptions: $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ be a $G^3$-valued random variable such that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically
conclusions: there exist random variables $T'_1, T'_2$ such that \begin{align*} \dist{T'_1}{T'_2} + & \eta (\dist{X_1^0}{T'_1} - \dist{X_1^0}{X_1}) + \eta(\dist{X_2^0}{T'_2} - \dist{X_2^0}{X_2}) \\ & \leqslant \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j = 1}^3 (\dist{X^0_i}{T_j} - \dist{X^0_i}{X_i}) \biggr). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: If $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ with total pairwise mutual information $\delta$, some conditioned pair has $\psi$-value at most $\delta$ plus controlled penalties.
nodes.label: lem:abstract

nodes.name: Definition of delta (7.5)
nodes.statement: \delta \coloneqq \sum_{1 \leqslant i < j \leqslant 3} \I{T_i;T_j}.
nodes.label: delta-t1t2t3-def

nodes.name: Proof of the abstract endgame lemma
nodes.statement: We apply the variant of the entropic Balog--Szemer\'edi--Gowers theorem stated in \Cref{lem-bsg}, taking $(A,B) = (T_1, T_2)$ there.
